summary:
Formula engine: keep the kit's own RK.expr (kit/core/rk.expr.js) and do not adopt a library.
- It has no eval or new Function and still works under a strict CSP. It was the fastest engine measured: 100k-row per-row eval in 14 ms, against 45–72 ms for math.js, expr-eval-fork and filtrex.
- It already has the bank-specific syntax: % literals, @params, backtick-quoted titles, aggregates, and n.m./n.a. handling.
- Add a function registry, plus an optional Excel financial-function pack from Formula.js 4.6.1 (MIT, UMD, CSP-safe; IRR, XNPV and PMT verified).
- Avoid expr-eval ≤2.0.2: CVE-2025-12735 is a remote-code-execution flaw rated 9.8.

Client query language: keep RK.query and treat its spec object as the single query format (intermediate representation) for charts, saved views and LLM output.
- Measured 17 ms at 10k rows, 45 ms at 100k and about 0.7 s at 1M rows for a 40-group group-by.

Optional SQL console: DuckDB-WASM.
- Pin 1.32.0 (wraps DuckDB 1.4.3). Gotcha: npm's 'latest' tag points to dev builds; 1.33.1-dev65.0 wraps DuckDB 1.5.6.
- It ran fully offline from a double-clicked file:// page using three tricks:
  - the ESM main module is shipped as a string and loaded with import() from a Blob URL, with its bare 'apache-arrow' import rewritten to the global Arrow 17 build;
  - the worker source is shipped as a string and started from a Blob URL;
  - the wasm is shipped as base64 inside a classic script and instantiated from a data: URL. A Blob URL fails because a worker started from file:// cannot fetch the page's Blob URLs.
- Cost: about 46 MB on disk and 2–4 s to start. Benefit: about 111 ms group-by and 50 ms median over 1M rows.
- Lock it down with enable_external_access=false plus lock_configuration=true, and use json_serialize_sql as a SELECT-only guard.
- sql.js is the light fallback (0.9 MB; pass wasmBinary on the first init call). It is slow beyond 100k rows.

Avoid AlaSQL for typed SQL: its double-backtick syntax runs arbitrary inline JavaScript (verified by the probe), and it needs eval. Arquero, AlaSQL and filtrex all fail under a strict CSP. The vendored ECharts 6.1 and Leaflet 1.9.4 pass, so a strict CSP is achievable for the whole kit.

Cross-filter: keep RK.store. It already has crossfilter semantics (each chart excludes its own filter). Use Mosaic as the architecture reference only; it ships only ESM source, needs DuckDB and has had breaking releases monthly. For scale, move to columnar storage with bitset filters, and switch to DuckDB above about 500k rows.

Local LLM: pages opened from file:// send Origin: null.
- Ollama's default allow-list includes file://*, which does not match null. Setting OLLAMA_ORIGINS=null makes Ollama panic at startup (from reading the gin-cors source; not tested against a live Ollama); only '*' or 'null*' work.
- vLLM now disables CORS by default. llama.cpp echoes any origin. LM Studio needs its CORS toggle.
- Chrome's Local Network Access prompt (Chrome 142+) behaviour for file:// pages is unspecified.
- Allowing null is equivalent to letting any website drive the local model API.
- Recommendation: a small Python companion that serves the report on 127.0.0.1 and proxies only the chat/models routes with a token.

The LLM should return JSON intents checked against a schema (query, metric, filter, data-only chart spec, read-only SQL), never code. They run locally, a strict CSP connect-src limits outbound requests to the LLM endpoint, and the model gets the schema and aggregates rather than raw rows.

Skills: use an Agent Skills SKILL.md for the LLM, plus an rk-skill.json manifest for declarative contributions, plus an optional classic-script skill.js. Code runs in a sandboxed srcdoc iframe (verified working on file://) over JSON-RPC via postMessage, modelled on MCP Apps.

libraries.name: DuckDB-WASM
libraries.capabilities: Full analytical SQL in browser: GROUP BY ALL, window, QUALIFY, PIVOT, quantile_cont/median, Arrow in/out; 1M-row group-by 111 ms, median 50 ms (measured).
libraries.offline_classic_script: No UMD. Verified file:// recipe: duckdb-browser.mjs as string -> import(blobURL) with 'apache-arrow' rewritten to global Arrow 17 UMD; duckdb-browser-eh.worker.js (classic) as string -> new Worker(blobURL); duckdb-eh.wasm as base64 classic script -> instantiate('data:application/wasm;base64,...'). Blob URL for wasm fails inside worker.
libraries.reason: Best engine for an optional, lazy-loaded SQL console power-pack (builder flag). Costs ~46 MB on disk and 2-4 s instantiate; needs 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; lock down with SET enable_external_access=false + lock_configuration=true; json_serialize_sql as SELECT-only guard; adapt BigInt/DECIMAL results; pin exact version (npm latest tag is a dev build).
libraries.size: eh.wasm 34.2 MB raw / 7.6 MB gz; worker 773 KB / 188 KB gz; mjs 32 KB

libraries.name: sql.js
libraries.capabilities: SQLite in wasm/asm.js; standard SQL incl. window functions; no median/quantile/PIVOT.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/sql-wasm.js + initSqlJs({wasmBinary}) from base64 classic script (verified 23-46 ms); dist/sql-asm.js needs no wasm and works under strict CSP. Default fetch of .wasm fails on file:// and the failed init promise is cached.
libraries.reason: Lightweight SQL fallback (~0.9 MB as b64 JS) when the size budget forbids DuckDB and data is <=100k rows; 1M rows is slow (2.4 s load + 3.3 s group-by measured).
libraries.size: sql-wasm.js 47 KB + wasm 658 KB (322 KB gz); sql-asm.js 1.36 MB (452 KB gz)

libraries.name: Arquero
libraries.capabilities: dplyr-style dataframe verbs (derive/filter/groupby/rollup/pivot/fold/join/window), Arrow I/O via flechette, streaming CSV/NDJSON readers.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/arquero.min.js (UMD, global aq); works on file://.
libraries.reason: Nice developer API and expression strings are restricted (no assignments/globals), but every verb compiles with new Function, so it fails under strict CSP (even groupby/rollup). Row-object ingest is slow (0.3-0.7 s per 1M rows). No push since 2025-05. Not needed for client queries given RK.query + DuckDB.

libraries.name: AlaSQL
libraries.capabilities: SQL over JS arrays (FROM ?), joins, subqueries, group-by, XLSX/CSV import; fast (1M-row group-by 101-148 ms measured).
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/alasql.min.js (min header still says 4.19.1).
libraries.reason: Double-backtick inline-JavaScript syntax executes arbitrary code (verified: SELECT VALUE ``window.x=1`` set a global); history of identifier code-injection advisories (Snyk SNYK-JS-ALASQL-1082932); compiles queries with new Function so fails strict CSP. Unsafe once SQL comes from LLMs, shared links or skills.

libraries.name: danfo.js
libraries.capabilities: pandas-like DataFrame/Series, groupby, IO, Plotly plotting.
libraries.offline_classic_script: lib/bundle.js exists but is 6.8 MB including TensorFlow.js.
libraries.reason: Huge bundle (TF.js), no release since 2025-04, nothing over RK.query/DuckDB.

libraries.name: Apache Arrow JS
libraries.capabilities: Arrow columnar tables, IPC read/write, tableFromArrays.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: Arrow.es2015.min.js (UMD, global Arrow); v17 build used for DuckDB recipe.
libraries.reason: Only as the DuckDB-WASM peer (must be v17 for 1.32.0); for plain data transport prefer flechette.

libraries.name: Flechette
libraries.capabilities: Fast, small Arrow IPC encode/decode to typed arrays.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/flechette.min.js (UMD); CSP-safe.
libraries.reason: Best option if the data contract or the future API moves to Arrow IPC (base64 in bundle.js); 3x smaller than apache-arrow.

libraries.name: Formula.js
libraries.capabilities: Excel function library: IRR, XIRR, NPV, XNPV, PMT, FV, RATE, date/stat/text functions (no parser).
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: lib/browser/formula.min.js (global formulajs); verified under strict CSP (IRR/XNPV/PMT).
libraries.reason: Plug into RK.expr via a function registry to give clients Excel-style financial functions without eval; permissive and small.

libraries.name: math.js
libraries.capabilities: Sandboxed expression parser, matrices, units, big numbers, symbolic functions.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: lib/browser/math.js (UMD, global math); CSP-safe (verified).
libraries.reason: Safe (import/createUnit disabled in evaluate) but over-powered for a metric box (user-defined functions, matrices) and 175 KB gz; slower than RK.expr (70 ms vs 14 ms per 100k rows).

libraries.name: expr-eval
libraries.capabilities: Math expression parser/evaluator.
libraries.offline_classic_script: dist/bundle.min.js (UMD).
libraries.reason: CVE-2025-12735 (CWE-94 RCE, CVSS 9.8) via crafted context/member in evaluate(); last npm release 2019.

libraries.name: expr-eval-fork
libraries.capabilities: Patched fork of expr-eval; stack-based evaluator.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/bundle.min.js (UMD, global exprEval); CSP-safe.
libraries.reason: Acceptable maintained fallback if an external expression engine is ever wanted; no IB syntax (%/params/quoted titles), slower than RK.expr.

libraries.name: filtrex
libraries.capabilities: Safe user-facing filter expressions compiled to JS.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/browser/filtrex.min.js.
libraries.reason: Compiles via new Function so fails strict CSP (verified); small project (92 stars), no release since 2024-10.

libraries.name: jsep
libraries.capabilities: Tiny JavaScript-expression parser to ESTree AST (no evaluation).
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/iife/jsep.iife.min.js; CSP-safe.
libraries.reason: Good base if RK.expr's parser is ever rewritten as a JS-subset dialect; evaluation must be self-written. Not needed now.

libraries.name: JSONata
libraries.capabilities: JSON query/transform language with aggregation.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: jsonata.min.js (UMD); CSP-safe (verified).
libraries.reason: Not for bankers' metrics, but useful for mapping a future data API's JSON to the dataset contract (adapter layer).

libraries.name: HyperFormula
libraries.capabilities: Full spreadsheet formula engine (Excel-compatible, dependency graph).
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (not evaluated further due to licence)
libraries.reason: GPL-3.0 / commercial dual licence is not acceptable for client deliverables.

libraries.name: PRQL (prqlc / prql-js)
libraries.capabilities: Pipelined query language compiled to SQL dialects.
libraries.offline_classic_script: No: wasm-bindgen ESM targets only; 5.5 MB wasm.
libraries.reason: A third language for clients, heavy wasm, still needs a SQL engine underneath; JS package renamed (prql-js stale since 2024-06).

libraries.name: Mosaic (vgplot/mosaic-core)
libraries.capabilities: Coordinator + Selections for scalable cross-filtering; query consolidation, caching, lineage-based pre-aggregation; DuckDB (wasm or Python/Go server) backend; vgplot grammar.
libraries.offline_classic_script: No: npm packages ship ESM/TS source only (src/*.js), no bundle; requires DuckDB + Arrow.
libraries.reason: Excellent architecture to copy (crossfilter Selection semantics, pre-aggregation for brushing) but monthly breaking releases (0.32 removed JSON transport, 0.32.1 removed WebSockets) and no classic build; RK.store already implements exclude-own-source crossfilter.
libraries.interactions_animation: Brush/interval/point selections, crossfilter resolution, linked views

libraries.name: crossfilter2
libraries.capabilities: Multidimensional filtering with dimensions/groups, incremental reduce.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: crossfilter.min.js.
libraries.reason: Stable but unmaintained since 2020; measured build 0.56 s / filter 0.18-0.23 s per 1M rows, no faster than hand-written loops; kit's RK.store already covers the semantics.

libraries.name: Perspective
libraries.capabilities: Streaming pivot engine (wasm) with ExprTK expression columns, datagrid and charts; originally J.P. Morgan.
libraries.offline_classic_script: No: ESM + wasm + worker; would need the same blob/data-URL recipe.
libraries.reason: Powerful pivot/expression engine for a possible 'data explorer' appendix, but heavy, ESM-only and has its own visual style; moved from finos to perspective-dev org.

libraries.name: WebLLM
libraries.capabilities: In-browser LLM inference on WebGPU; OpenAI-style chat API, JSON-schema constrained output, function calling, Web/Service Worker engines, Cache/IndexedDB/OPFS caches.
libraries.offline_classic_script: No: ESM lib/index.js (6.8 MB). WebGPU and Cache API are available on file:// (secure context) but model weights must be fetched over http(s).
libraries.reason: Only for companion/intranet-served mode where weights are hosted; GB-scale weights cannot be bundled into a double-click report.
libraries.size: 6.8 MB raw / 2.3 MB gz + model weights (GB)

libraries.name: transformers.js
libraries.capabilities: ONNX Runtime Web/WebGPU inference for embeddings, classification, small generative models.
libraries.offline_classic_script: No: dist/transformers.web.min.js is ESM; ORT wasm fetched; small models could be embedded via data: URL like DuckDB.
libraries.reason: Useful later for small on-page tasks such as semantic search over the metric/field catalog with a ~20-25 MB embedding model.
libraries.size: 454 KB raw / 128 KB gz + ORT wasm

libraries.name: wllama
libraries.capabilities: llama.cpp compiled to wasm; CPU inference of GGUF models; can load a user-picked local GGUF File/Blob.
libraries.offline_classic_script: No (ESM); works conceptually on file:// via user file pick, but single-threaded there (no SharedArrayBuffer without COOP/COEP).
libraries.reason: Only fully-offline in-page LLM option without a server, but single-thread CPU makes 7B models impractical.

libraries.name: Ollama
libraries.capabilities: Local LLM server with native API and OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions (streaming, tools, response_format), JSON-schema structured outputs, embeddings.
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (local server). From file:// pages Chrome sends Origin: null; default allow-list (incl. file://*) does not match; OLLAMA_ORIGINS=null panics gin-cors validation; use '*' or 'null*' (from reading the source, not tested against a live Ollama).
libraries.reason: Reference local endpoint for Step 2 behind an OpenAI-compatible provider abstraction; prefer reaching it through a Python companion proxy (same origin, allow-listed routes, token), because allowing the null origin exposes /api/pull and /api/delete to any website via sandboxed iframes.

libraries.name: VMind
libraries.capabilities: LLM-driven chart generation/editing producing VChart specs; data extraction/insight; GIF/video export.
libraries.offline_classic_script: build/index.min.js UMD exists but expects Node-module globals (util, stream, http...); 2.1 MB min.
libraries.reason: Outputs VChart specs (kit uses ECharts), heavy, last release 2025-08; borrow the prompt -> spec -> render/edit loop only.

libraries.name: GPT-Vis
libraries.capabilities: 26 chart types from an LLM-friendly markdown-like DSL ('vis line' + indented data), streaming rendering, fault tolerance; G2/G6 based; companion MCP server and chart-visualization Agent Skill.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/umd/index.min.js (global GPTVis), 2.3 MB.
libraries.reason: Borrow the DSL/streaming/fault-tolerance design for the kit's own rk-chart intent schema; the visual style is not pitchbook-grade and it is a second chart engine.

libraries.name: LIDA
libraries.capabilities: Python: data summarisation, goal generation, visualisation code generation/execution, self-evaluation and repair, infographics.
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (Python)
libraries.reason: Useful pipeline ideas (summarise -> goals -> viz -> evaluate), but its generate-and-execute-code model is unsuitable for client deliverables; inactive.

libraries.name: NL4DV
libraries.capabilities: Python: NL query -> structured JSON (attributes, analytic tasks, Vega-Lite specs); LLM mode.
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (Python)
libraries.reason: Its structured-intent JSON output is exactly the recommended LLM contract (intents validated by schema, executed locally).

libraries.name: Data Formulator
libraries.capabilities: AI-agent data exploration app: data connectors, concept-driven derived fields, branching Data Threads, charts.
libraries.offline_classic_script: n/a (application)
libraries.reason: UX reference for derived-metric creation and branching exploration history in the chat panel.

libraries.name: MCP Apps (ext-apps)
libraries.license: npm says MIT; README badge says Apache-2.0 (verify before reusing code)
libraries.capabilities: Standard for interactive UIs from MCP tools: ui:// resources (text/html;profile=mcp-app) rendered in sandboxed iframes, JSON-RPC 2.0 over postMessage, host-enforced CSP from declared domains, sandbox proxy for web hosts.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Protocol reference; the sandboxed srcdoc iframe + postMessage pattern was verified to work on file://.
libraries.reason: Model for the skills sandbox protocol (page = host, skill iframe = client, permission-gated methods), enabling the same skill UIs to run in Claude/ChatGPT and in reports later.

libraries.name: QuickJS-emscripten
libraries.capabilities: QuickJS JavaScript interpreter in wasm with memory limits and interrupt handlers for running untrusted code.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Singlefile variants embed the wasm (@jitl/quickjs-singlefile-browser-release-sync, ESM ~0.6-0.8 MB); needs blob import on file://.
libraries.reason: For deterministic, resource-limited execution of untrusted skill JS when a sandboxed iframe or worker is not enough; avoid SES lockdown (intrusive) and Pyodide (size, MPL-2.0).

key_insights: file:// facts measured in Chromium 141 headless: origin is 'null', isSecureContext=true, no SharedArrayBuffer. fetch/XHR of local files, new Worker(file) and import(file) are all blocked. Blob workers and import(blobURL) work. A blob worker cannot fetch the page's blob URLs but can fetch data: URLs (30 MB tested). IndexedDB, localStorage and the Cache API work; OPFS throws SecurityError. Sandboxed srcdoc iframes work and cannot read the parent.

The general recipe for any ESM + worker + wasm library on file:// is: ship the ESM source as a string in a classic script and load it with import() from a Blob URL, rewriting bare imports to UMD globals; ship the worker source as a string and start it from a Blob URL; ship the wasm as base64 in a classic script and pass it as a data:application/wasm URL. Verified with DuckDB-WASM 1.32.0.

Raw on-disk size, not gzip size, is the load cost on file://, because browsers do not decompress local files. Example: the DuckDB power-pack is about 46 MB as base64 and needs 2-4 s to instantiate, so it must be lazy-loaded behind a builder flag.

A strict CSP without unsafe-eval breaks Arquero, AlaSQL and filtrex. It does not break RK.expr, sql.js asm, math.js, expr-eval-fork, jsep, JSONata, Formula.js, ECharts 6.1.0 or Leaflet 1.9.4. Emit a strict meta CSP from the builder, with connect-src limited to the LLM endpoint, to make data exfiltration by a prompt-injected LLM impossible (verified that external fetch is blocked). Add a CSP smoke test for every vendored library.

The kit's existing RK.expr beat every library on safety, speed (14 ms per 100k rows) and domain syntax. Extend it with a function registry, IB window functions (lag, pct_change, cagr, rank) and Formula.js financial functions, rather than replacing it.

Use the RK.query spec object (from, select[{expr, as, format}], by, where, sort, limit) as the single query format for charts, saved views, LLM intents and engines. RK.query executes it by default; it compiles to DuckDB SQL when the power-pack is on.

Before reaching for DuckDB, columnar internal storage (typed arrays, dictionary-encoded strings, per-filter bitsets) would bring RK.query from about 0.7 s to about 0.15-0.25 s at 1M rows. Also consider a columnar or Arrow-IPC-base64 option in the data contract.

DuckDB-WASM gotchas: the npm 'latest' tag is a dev build; 1.32.0 requires apache-arrow 17; BIGINT results come back as BigInt and break JSON.stringify; DECIMAL comes back as strings; the COI bundle is unusable on file://. To harden it: SET enable_external_access=false; SET lock_configuration=true; and use json_serialize_sql to reject anything that is not a SELECT.
AlaSQL's double-backtick syntax is an arbitrary-JavaScript execution surface (verified), so never feed it untrusted, LLM-generated or shared SQL.

Local LLM CORS: pages opened from file:// send Origin: null, plus a preflight because of the JSON content type.
- Ollama: its default file://* entry does not match null. OLLAMA_ORIGINS=null panics in gin-cors Validate; use '*' or 'null*'. This is from reading the source, not a live test.
- vLLM: --allowed-origins now defaults to [].
- llama.cpp: echoes any origin, with credentials.
- LM Studio: needs its 'Enable CORS' toggle.
- Allowing null effectively allows any website, via sandboxed iframes.

Chrome Local Network Access (142+; split in 145 into local-network and loopback-network permissions) gates requests to loopback. Its behaviour for file:// pages is 'weakly specified', so test it on the bank's browser or push the LocalNetworkAccessAllowedForUrls policy. A Python companion serving the report on 127.0.0.1 and proxying only the chat/models routes avoids CORS, LNA and admin-endpoint exposure, and unlocks fetch, ES modules and workers.

LLM contract: the model returns JSON intents constrained by a schema (query, metric, filter, data-only rk-chart spec, read-only SQL, answer) through response_format or tools on any OpenAI-compatible server. The page validates them locally (RK.expr.check / RK.query.parse / the SQL guard), executes them, shows the editable formula, and feeds errors back to the model for at most 2 retries.
- Never let the model write ECharts options or HTML formatters, and never put LLM text into innerHTML.
- Send the schema, data dictionary and aggregates, not raw rows, and keep an audit log in IndexedDB.

Text-to-chart references: GPT-Vis has an LLM-friendly streaming DSL and NL4DV has structured JSON intents; LIDA generates and executes code, which is unsafe. Local text-to-SQL candidates for IT: Arctic-Text2SQL-R1 (7B-32B), Qwen3-Coder, DuckDB-NSQL (on Ollama). For the kit's own query dialect, few-shot examples in the system prompt matter more than a SQL-specialised model.

Skills: follow the open Agent Skills format for the LLM-facing part. SKILL.md frontmatter has name (64 chars max, lowercase and hyphens, must match the folder) and description (1024 chars max), with optional license, compatibility, metadata and allowed-tools. Loading is progressive: name and description, then the body (under 500 lines), then references.
- Add an rk-skill.json manifest for runtime contributions (functions, metrics, queries, charts, prompts, tools, permissions) and an optional classic-script skill.js wrapper for file://.
- Imported (untrusted) skills get declarative contributions only; their code runs in a sandboxed srcdoc iframe with an inner CSP and no network, over JSON-RPC via postMessage modelled on MCP Apps.

In-browser LLMs: WebGPU is available on file://, but WebLLM and transformers.js weights must be fetched over http(s), so they suit companion or intranet mode only. wllama can load a user-picked GGUF on file:// but runs single-threaded. Chrome's Prompt API status for web pages in 2026 is contested and it is Chrome-only, so offer it only as an optional extra.
